**Release unused delayed acquisitions before finishing.** If cancellation arrives before the countdown starts, or either journal save fails, `acquisition` is not invoked and `released` is not called. `selectingId_` and the active operation slot remain reserved. Later interactive captures can fail with `busy_selecting` until the resident restarts. Keep a release callback for the delayed branch and call it before each early return. Once acquisition starts, leave release to the countdown and adapter.

In the delayed branch of OperationService, retain a one-shot release callback for the unused acquisition and invoke it before each early return that occurs before acquisition begins, including both save failures and cancellation or early-error exits. ✅ Addressed in commit bde5461

Confirmed and fixed in bde54614a. A delayed capture reserved the selection before any adapter held it, so an operation that ended before its countdown started (a cancel in that gap, either journal save failing) never released it. The operation service now keeps the release for that branch and calls it before each of those early exits, ahead of `finish()`, which only frees the selection once no owner is left. New contract test `cancellingBeforeTheCountdownStartsFreesTheSelection` cancels inside the acceptance reply and then runs another interactive capture, which must not be `busy_selecting`.

@patrick-hudson Thanks for the fix. The supplied code releases the unused reservation on both journal-save failures and on early exits before acquisition starts. I did not run the reported regression test. ---

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Add `session_locked` to the accepted helper error codes.** In `src/capture/main.cpp` (lines 215-217), a delayed live region forwards the `source.delayed()` error to `finish(error)`. When the screen is locked at expiry, that error is `SourceAdapter::lockedError()`, so the helper sends an `error` frame with code `session_locked`. The `allowed` list in `receive()` (line 187) does not contain `session_locked`. The controller therefore treats the frame as `fail(unavailable("capture_protocol","error_frame"))` and kills the helper. The user sees a generic "could not complete source acquisition" protocol failure instead of the lock message. The diagnostics log also records a protocol fault. Nothing is captured, so the privacy property holds. `WaylandRegionProcess` added `session_locked` to its own list for the same case. Add it here, and consider `delay_unavailable` too.
🐛 Proposed fix (line 187)

```diff - const auto code=payload["code"].toString();const QStringList allowed{"cancelled","display_changed","capture_target","capture_unavailable","capture_geometry","capture_failed","capture_timeout","input_excessive","image_limit","encoding_failed","capture_io"}; + const auto code=payload["code"].toString();const QStringList allowed{"cancelled","display_changed","capture_target","capture_unavailable","capture_geometry","capture_failed","capture_timeout","input_excessive","image_limit","encoding_failed","capture_io","session_locked","delay_unavailable"}; ```

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Report delay-save failures against the correct action.** The error callback always calls `showActionFailure("region", ...)`. The lambda is created inside the per-action loop, so it can capture `action` instead. A failed save from the Window, Monitor, or Desktop menu then gets shown as a Region failure. For `output_required`, this opens Capture settings with the region exception highlighted.
Proposed fix

```diff - connect(choice,&QAction::triggered,this,[this,seconds]{ + connect(choice,&QAction::triggered,this,[this,seconds,action]{ ... - session_.saveAsync(document,session_.revision(),[this](Result result){if(!result)showActionFailure("region",result.error);}); + session_.saveAsync(document,session_.revision(),[this,action](Result result){if(!result)showActionFailure(action,result.error);}); ```
